items.quote: The LinkedIn API uses OAuth 2.0 for member (user) authorization and API authentication.
items.why: States LinkedIn API uses OAuth 2.0 for API authentication, matching oauth2 method.

items.quote: Not all APIs support Application Authorization. For example, Marketing APIs you must use Member Authorization explained above.
items.why: Says Marketing APIs require Member Authorization; no oauth2 statement or 2-legged detail.

items.quote: Visit your app's Product tab in the Developer Portal to apply for the Advertising API product.
items.why: Shows where to apply for Advertising API; does not state approval gate.

items.quote: LinkedIn reserves the right to review applications and select partners at its discretion and a partner might not be upgraded even if they meet these minimum requirements.
items.why: LinkedIn reviews applications at its discretion; matches admin review gate.

items.quote: All applications start with Development tier. You must apply separately to upgrade to the Standard tier.
items.why: Confirms Development tier start and separate Standard upgrade application; no approval gate stated.

items.quote: The platform offers APIs to create LinkedIn marketing campaigns, to report campaign performance, to manage leads, and to grow a company Page.
items.why: Lists campaign, reporting, lead and Page APIs; no REST, versioning or breadth detail.

items.quote: With Advertising APIs, streamline your campaign management, audience targeting, and track performance to optimize advertising efforts.
items.why: Says Advertising APIs manage campaigns, audience targeting and track performance; leads not mentioned.

items.quote: MCP server for the LinkedIn Marketing API — campaigns, analytics, creatives, from any MCP client. MIT.
items.why: Describes an MCP server for LinkedIn Marketing API under MIT; no URL or official status.
Directly states no official LinkedIn MCP, matching vendor-official False; existence not covered.
